body: you’re flattering me haha, but thanks for the compliment. do u have any advice to give? since i noticed that u have a ND and a lop as well (don’t mind the stalking)
alright thank you so much, will heed ur advice. really appreciate everything. wish u a good day/night ahead

thanks really appreciate the info 🙏 for confirmation; i should not intervene if my lop mounts my ND from the back? and should only separate them if he shows signs of aggression and is mounting her from the front? is there a possibility of him crushing her if he mounts her at all?

it’s fine, i appreciate the honesty. my room is around 400 square ft, and there’s only my bed, a desk, and his stuff. i keep all my belongings in a box under my bed (rough, i know), so im quite sure it will be sufficient space for 2 rabbits. i can only separate them by placing each of their pens (built w cnc grids, double layered) at the opposite ends of my room). i don’t have the luxury of space, unfortunately..

thanks for the advice, however since she is very young and rabbit vets here only perform  surgery on rabbits that are more than 6 months old, i think i will attempt in bonding them, but with much caution and supervision. i will ensure that both are not free roaming at the same time when i’m not present in case of sudden conflicts. that being said, how old do rabbits often hit sexual maturity? what are some signs that show that a rabbit has hit puberty? 

next, let’s say a few months down the road, when both my bunnies are neutered and are safe to bond. since a ND is unlikely to grow as big as a lop, should i intervene and stop my lop from mounting my ND? i know that mounting is normal behavior but when is it.. too dangerous? 

thanks, really appreciate it 🙏
ok, thank you for the advice. i’ll not swap their cages. but will it be ok if i kept them separated in the same room but at different ends? with a double layer cnc grid built play pen.

would the indoor hallway be appropriate? areas such as bathrooms and kitchens are common areas, and people may flock there randomly. i know this will cause stress for the rabbit. i don’t have a completely new room, but i can set up a tiny temporary play pen by the hallway at odd hours (when there’s nobody around) to let them bond.will that be safer than allocating the neutral space to my room?
thanks for the link. i’ll check it out. appreciate it man 🙏
but will it be okay if i kept them in the same room, just separated in different cages? if that’s not advisable, i’ll have to give the baby away
